paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Israel never had to guess. The cloud was over the tabernacle by day and looked like fire at night, and "At the LORD’s command the Israelites set out, and at the LORD’s command they camped" (Numbers 9:18). Two days, a month or longer, they stayed put until it lifted (Numbers 9:22). Then they went, whether it was day or night (Numbers 9:21).

This passage is about following God's lead, and following means staying AND going. Waiting is hard when the cloud sits there for a long time. Packing up is hard when you just finished unpacking. I think either one can feel like a lot, and God's people did both the same way, because the command was His (Numbers 9:23). So when you're in a season of waiting or a season of moving, you can ask what the Lord is saying, not what you feel like doing.

And He didn't leave them to figure it out alone. He gave Moses, Israel's leader, two silver trumpets so His people could hear the call: gather, move, remember (Numbers 10:2). He even said that in battle, the trumpets would bring them "remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies" (Numbers 10:9). Then He signed it: "I am the LORD your God" (Numbers 10:10). He leads you, He hears you, and He is the One you're following, so you can trust Him on the days you stay and the days you go.
